newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD reprimands S.Korea amid union crackdown.
newsitem.headline: OECD reprimands S.Korea amid union crackdown.

text.p: OECD chief Donald Johnston said on Friday he was worried about the turmoil triggered by new labour laws in South Korea and had reminded Seoul's envoy in Paris of the organisation's commitment to respect for human rights.

South Korea became the 29th member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development in December and the OECD said Johnston had used the occasion of a first meeting with the new Korean envoy to express concern and dismay among its members.

A statement issued by the free-market organisation said the labour laws, which sparked strikes, threats of even wider protest and a showdown between striking union leaders and the Seoul authorities, would be reviewed by the OECD on January 22.

"Pending that review, Mr Johnston did not comment on the content of the new legislation but recalled the commitment made by Korea and stressed the fundamental importance that the organisation attaches to respect for human rights and the democratic process," the statement said.
It was issued after South Korea's ambassador to the OECD, Bohn-Young Koo, met Johnston, who is secretary general of the organisation, for the first time since South Korea became a member.

It also came on the day that a court in South Korea issued arrest warrants for seven striking union leaders holed up in a cathedral. The unrest has been sparked by adoption of a bill allowing worker layoffs for the first time.

"He (Johnston) also reminded Ambassador Koo that over the past year various OECD member countries have registered their dissatisfaction, in particular with the imprisonment in Korea of union leaders for their union activities," the OECD statement said.
"OECD members voiced concerns during Korea's accession process with industrial relations in Korea."
It added: "The Korean government undertook to reform its legislation in line with internationally accepted standards, including such basic rights as freedom of association and collective bargaining."
